hypothesis: Bare fails because the 7B reads circuits row by row (8 queries each, so C is barely touched) and then writes malformed or answer-contradicting 24-bit strings. If the harness enumerates the rule-allowed circuits itself (3 inputs reduce to 1 output, so each circuit has exactly two AND/OR gates plus NOTs; the inventory is split without replacement), shows the model the surviving candidates and which inputs still split them, re-asks on zero-information queries, and builds the final string from the model's per-circuit candidate picks, then every episode ends with all three circuits pinned to a single rule-consistent table within 18 queries, and the returned guess equals those tables. Falsified if any episode ends with >1 candidate for some circuit, a guess that contradicts an observed answer, or an observed answer that eliminates every candidate (which would show the rule reading is wrong).
behavior_changes: Harness enumerates the hypothesis space from the system prompt's rules and inventory (8 / 52 / 63 tables per circuit for the inventories in this batch), coupled across A/B/C through the gate split, and filters it by the answers so far. If the answers ever contradict the space, it falls back to any non-constant table consistent with the answers.

Each turn, the model gets a fresh, compact context (system prompt + one user message): all answers, per-circuit status (SOLVED with its table and expression / candidate list / count), and up to 8 informative queries with their 1/0 split counts, sorted by evenness. The growing chat transcript is gone.

Replies with no parsable query, a repeated query, a query on a solved circuit, or a query that can't split any candidates are re-asked with a specific reason, up to 4 tries. Re-asks don't spend budget. If every try is uninformative, the model's own first valid query is sent anyway; the harness never writes a query.
Querying stops early once every circuit has a single candidate.

Final phase: the model picks a numbered candidate per circuit ('A: k, B: k, C: k') and/or writes a 24-bit guess. The harness assembles the 24 bits from those picks, accepting only rule- and answer-consistent tables, re-asking on bad picks, and falling back to the candidate closest to what the model wrote.
preserved_behaviors: Frozen solver: only self.llm is called. Label-free: only env.query / history / inventory / system_prompt are used. audit.py reports OK in the scratch arm.
The model chooses every query sent to the environment.
The benchmark's system prompt is still sent verbatim, and the final output is a single <guess> with 24 bits in A,B,C row order.
verification: Label-free audit of bare's traces: only 4/10 final guesses are 24 bits and consistent with bare's own answers (2 missing, 3 the wrong length (20/26/32 bits), 4 contradict 2-11 observed answers). Bare spends 8 queries per circuit and reaches C with 1-2 queries left.
Replayed all 10 bare query histories through the enumerated space: no history eliminated all candidates (relaxed fallback never triggered). The rule reading held on 180 real answers.

Ran check_b0r0_cand_pilot_strict_b10g3r2_b0r0g2.py twice (before and after a menu-wording fix): 10/10 status=ok, 10/10 parsed guesses, 0 crashes. Final run used 6-18 queries (mean 10.7), 8-19 LLM calls.

Replayed each final-run history: every instance ends with exactly 1 candidate for A, B and C, and the returned guess equals those tables on 10/10. The model's final reply was 'A: 1, B: 1, C: 1' plus a matching <guess> each time, so the fallback was never used. For i105, i128 and i250, run 1 (different query paths) produced identical tables.

Disagreement with bare on i98, settled by evidence: bare guessed A(1,1,1)=1 without querying it; this candidate queried A(1,1,1) and the environment answered 0. Bare's A and B chunks are also outside the rule-allowed space. Its i98 guess is refuted even though it matched its own 18 answers.

Read the traces: the model's queries come from the listed menu with plausible reasoning. Re-asks fire when it picks rows every candidate agrees on (e.g. B(1,1,1) and A(0,0,0) in i128), and it recovers on the next try.
risks: Thin budget margin on NOT-bearing inventories: i250 needed all 18 queries and i247 needed 17, because the model doesn't always take the most even split. A harder instance could end with 2+ candidates for a circuit, leaving the final choice to the model.

Correctness depends on reading the rules as: all gates are used; exactly two binary gates per circuit; NOT allowed anywhere, including on the output; constant circuits excluded. The replay supports this reading, but the hidden tables were never seen. If the real generator is narrower, uniqueness may be declared later than necessary (safe). If it's wider, a wrong table could be declared SOLVED. The relaxed fallback triggers only on outright contradiction.
The informative-query menu and the 'SOLVED' labels push much of the deduction into the harness. The model still writes every query and pick, but its contribution is mostly choosing from the menu.
Inventories with many NOTs would enlarge the enumeration (cheap at this scale) and the candidate lists; lists over 8 (in-loop) or 12 (final) are summarized rather than shown.
